sources.title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models? — quoted full-text passages (arXiv 2508.17536v2 PDF)

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The authors split multi-agent debate (MAD) into majority voting and inter-agent debate and, across seven NLP benchmarks, find that majority voting alone accounts for most of the gains usually attributed to MAD. They model debate as a stochastic process, prove it induces a martingale over agents' beliefs so that debate alone does not improve expected correctness, and show that interventions biasing belief updates toward correction improve debate.
title: Majority voting, not inter-agent debate, accounts for most multi-agent debate gains
